## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: f2dbecb84ec45427f76bf02fc29fa1a8b2c9dd2e

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** I traced the history of `PageManager.java` with `git log -p --follow`, searching for when `doFinalWorkForPopPageInternal` (the method touched by the fix) was introduced, since the fix commit only rearranges code between the "immediate" section of `popPageInternal` and this helper method. Only one commit besides the fix ever touches `doFinalWorkForPopPageInternal`: `f2dbecb8` ("refacoted PageManager to better support per-Page transition animations..."). I confirmed no intermediate commits (`3c476c4`, `9927741`, `04e9849`, `c1150c9`, `a138660`, `66126f4`, etc.) modified this method.

**(2) The specific change:** Before `f2dbecb8`, `popPageInternal` did:
```java
mContainerView.removeView(removedPage.getView());
removedPage.onDetach();
mCurPage = prevPage;   // set immediately
```
and only deferred `onHidden()`/`onUncovered()` behind the animation delay.

In `f2dbecb8`, this was refactored so that `mContainerView.removeView(...)`, `removedPage.onDetach()`, and critically `mCurPage = prevPage` were all moved into the new `doFinalWorkForPopPageInternal()` method, which is only invoked either immediately (no animation) or after `animationDuration` via `postDelayed` (when animated). This means when popping the last page with a transition animation, `mCurPage` remains stale (pointing at the removed page) for the entire animation duration instead of becoming `null`/`prevPage` right away.

**(3) Evidence:** The fix commit `8e17c7c` does exactly the inverse of `f2dbecb8`'s change — it moves `mContainerView.removeView(removedPage.getView());` and `mCurPage = prevPage;` back out of `doFinalWorkForPopPageInternal` into the immediate/unconditional part of `popPageInternal`, restoring the pre-`f2dbecb8` behavior while keeping the newer animation-callback structure for `onDetach`/`onHidden`/`onUncovered`. This is a near-exact reversal of the change introduced in `f2dbecb8`, strongly indicating it as the bug's origin.

I'm reasonably confident in this identification since the diffs are direct inverses of each other and no other commit touched the relevant code path in between.
